rubrics.criterion: The signal teardown path no longer performs the session-exit transition (storing the exit flag, posting the wakeup semaphore, recording the error) as direct surgery on the session record: the transition is requested through an interface of the session module or performed inside the session implementation, while the signal module retains only signal concerns (its registration guard, its debug log line, and the negative-signal backtrace-and-abort policy).
rubrics.rationale: This is the relocation the task's teardown observation points at; the starting tree's transitional helper put the whole transition, including the error write, in the signal module.

rubrics.criterion: The single-threaded request loop consults the session through the session module's interfaces for both its exit polling and its exit result: no raw atomic access to the session's exit flag in the loop head, and no direct reads of the session's recorded error or its io_uring pool to derive what the loop returns (a session-side loop-result function, or equivalent session-owned exit-status and result interfaces, both count).
rubrics.rationale: The loop-head flag poll and the result/error/uring combination in the tail are the two places this loop negotiates the session's lifecycle state; both must be session-side in a sound repair.

rubrics.criterion: The multi-thread loop's shutdown sequencing is session-side for the parts that are session business: waiting until the session is exited and the accompanying shutdown debug message are requested from (or performed by) the session module rather than by direct member surgery from the loop module. Taking the worker-list lock directly around the loop module's own worker-cancel walk is acceptable.
rubrics.rationale: The shutdown conversation (park-on-semaphore, log under session debug, lock the worker list) was packed into a loop-module helper; only the cancel walk over its own local worker list is genuinely loop business.

rubrics.criterion: The mount module no longer decides the session's channel state by writing the session record: adopting the auto-unmount fd into the session, publishing the channel fd and mountpoint after a successful mount, and the failure-path channel invalidation (fd, recorded error, sync-init flag) all happen inside the session implementation or behind session-owned interfaces, so the mount code keeps only mount mechanics.
rubrics.rationale: The starting tree handed the session's mount-channel decisions (socket adoption, publish, invalidation) to the mount module; returning them to the session owner is the core of this location.

rubrics.criterion: No resolution-by-cosmetics: the teardown, loop and mount code does not merely rename or reshape its local helpers while keeping the same direct member surgery on session fields inside the consumer modules (e.g., the same flag store, semaphore post and error write re-wrapped in another local helper of the same module, or the loop simply inlining what its helper did).
rubrics.rationale: A rename or re-wrap that leaves lifecycle decisions in the loop/signal/mount modules fails the task even though it compiles and tests green.

rubrics.criterion: No behavior was deleted to make the refactor easier: waking the parked loops on session exit is preserved, the negative-signal backtrace-and-abort path is preserved, io_uring teardown on loop exit is preserved, and the loop result discipline is not weakened (the length of the last read request is still never returned as the loop result).
rubrics.rationale: These are the observable behaviors a sloppy relocation would most plausibly drop; their absence marks a behavior-changing, not behavior-preserving, repair.

rubrics.criterion: New session-module interfaces that are used across translation units are declared in the library's private (library-internal) header, and functions added to the session implementation that only one file needs are kept file-local rather than needlessly exported into that shared header.
rubrics.rationale: The tree splits declarations between the library's private header and file-local statics; a repair that respects this layout stays in-house without widening the internal surface.

rubrics.criterion: Cross-module declarations the refactor made unnecessary are removed together with the code that used them: no prototypes, forward declarations or extra includes remain in the mount-internal header for mount-side session operations that no longer exist, and no stale transitional comments describe the hand-rolled arrangement at the rewired call sites.
rubrics.rationale: The starting tree grew a paired mount-side session API with its own header exposure; a complete repair removes that exposure once the decisions return to the session module.

rubrics.criterion: The public surface is untouched: no edits to headers under the library's public include directory, no new symbols exported from the shared library, and no changes to the symbol version script or the versioned compatibility entry points.
rubrics.rationale: The task fixes an internal responsibility split in a system library that ships a stable ABI; any public-surface movement is a compatibility break.

rubrics.criterion: The refactor leaves no dead scaffolding behind the transition: the auxiliaries the starting tree added to the signal, loop and mount modules are gone (absorbed into the session module or deleted outright) unless they remain live and reduced to session-interface calls, and every declaration that survives is still referenced.
rubrics.rationale: The injected state deliberately carries transitional helpers; whether they end up moved, dissolved or deleted, leftover husks are unrepaired residue.

rubrics.criterion: No editing-process artifacts are left in the tree: commented-out copies of the replaced code, backup or conflict files (.orig, .rej, .bak, *.patch.htm), stray debug printfs, or test/playground files added during the refactor.
rubrics.rationale: A cleanup task spanning five library files invites exactly this residue; it is graded as unsanitary deliverable state.

rubrics.criterion: Teardown-signal semantics survive intact: receiving a teardown signal still marks the session exited, wakes loops parked on the session's semaphore, and records the signal value as the session error; with session debug set the teardown message is still logged; a negative signal value still prints the assertion error, dumps the backtrace, and aborts.
rubrics.rationale: These guarantees cross exactly the seam being refactored; the relocation must not silently reorder or drop any of them.

rubrics.criterion: Mount-channel bookkeeping survives intact: success still publishes the channel fd and mountpoint to the session before the early-daemonize 'mounted' notification; failure still closes the channel fd before invalidating the session channel state, records the error, and clears the sync-init flag; the auto-unmount comm socket is still kept only when auto-unmount was requested and the mount succeeded, otherwise closed with the fusermount child reaped; helper-spawn failure on the direct-mount path still unmounts the mount fd.
rubrics.rationale: The socket-adoption and reap/unmount rules encode the auto-unmount contract the starting tree documents in its comments; they encode when the helper unmounts the filesystem and are regression-sensitive.

rubrics.criterion: Worker shutdown discipline survives intact: the loop still waits for the session to be exited before cancelling exactly the registered workers with the worker-list lock held and then joining them, and the loop configuration semantics (clone-fd behavior, idle and max thread counts) are unchanged.
rubrics.rationale: Moving 'wait, log, lock' across the module boundary risks canceling workers while the list can still change; the lock-hold window and join order are the regression-sensitive core.

rubrics.criterion: Session debug logging still behaves the same in the repointed paths: the teardown log line is emitted under the same condition (session debug flag set), and the multi-thread shutdown message remains a debug-level message emitted when the session has been flagged exited.
rubrics.rationale: Logging side effects are the observable difference several tests and operators rely on; a relocation that detaches the log conditions from the session's exit state changes behavior without failing every test.
